rho and theta are the two scalar arguments of phi and are used as real polar coordinates; neither is an R^2 vector.
The point has two coordinates and is passed to g defined on R^2; the one-dimensional domain is incompatible with both facts.
An antiderivative of exp(-t/2) is -2 exp(-t/2), so evaluation from 1 to infinity gives 2 exp(-1/2), not one-half exp(-1/2).
The preceding perturbation estimate and cited inverse criterion yield the bound only after left multiplication by T_n inverse; this also supplies the stated nonsingularity conclusion.
The convolution was defined from f and g, and expanding its integral gives one factor of each; repeating f would erase g from the asserted identity.
The closing parenthesis has no opening partner inside the integral and is a typographical delimiter error.
